Build a pseudo-spectra MGF from a grouped xcms object

Source: R/api.R
process_xcms.Rd

Multi-sample route. Every feature in featureDefinitions() gets one MGF block, built from its top-top_n most intense samples. Run it in one call (stage = "all") or one stage at a time so a scheduler can parallelize the per-sample and per-batch work.

Usage

process_xcms(
  input,
  output = NULL,
  tmp_dir = NULL,
  stage = c("all", "prepare", "sample", "filter", "finalize"),
  sample_idx = NULL,
  sample_file = NULL,
  subsample = FALSE,
  subset_size = 100L,
  q_prob = 0.9,
  top_n = 10L,
  ppm = 20,
  rt_buffer = 5,
  grouper = NULL,
  group_statistics_fn = NULL,
  filter_fn = NULL,
  fdr_thresh = 0.1,
  cor_thresh = 0.1,
  min_count = 10L,
  batch_idx = NULL,
  n_batches = 1L,
  ion_mode = "POSITIVE",
  ...
)

Arguments

input

An XcmsExperiment/XCMSnExp (after xcms::groupChromPeaks()), or a .rds / .qs / .rda path to one. Only read by prepare.

output

MGF path. Required for "all" and "finalize".

tmp_dir

Working directory. NULL is only allowed for stage = "all", which then uses a tempfile() deleted on exit.

stage

One of "all", "prepare", "sample", "filter", "finalize".

sample_idx

Row of manifest.csv to process at "sample". Takes precedence over sample_file.

sample_file

mzML basename to process at "sample"; looked up in manifest.csv.

subsample

If TRUE, keep subset_size samples chosen by apricot MaxCoverageSelection (needs Python with apricot-select and numpy). See subset_samples_xcms().

subset_size, q_prob

Passed to subset_samples_xcms().

top_n

Number of most intense samples per feature to extract. Used by prepare only.

ppm

Used twice: at sample, the MS1 m/z tolerance for the precursor trace (converted to Da at the sample's largest feature m/z); and for the default grouper ppm_upgma(ppm = ppm).

rt_buffer

Seconds added to both sides of each peak's rtmin/rtmax at sample.

grouper

A grouper closure (see grouper-contract); NULL uses ppm_upgma(ppm = ppm).

group_statistics_fn

A statistics closure (see stats-contract); NULL uses correlation_statistics(min_count = min_count).

filter_fn

A filter closure (see filter-contract); NULL uses correlation_filtering(cor_thresh, fdr_thresh).

fdr_thresh, cor_thresh, min_count

Only used to build the default filter_fn / group_statistics_fn.

batch_idx, n_batches

For "filter": process slice batch_idx (1-based) of n_batches. A slice past the last feature writes an empty parquet.

ion_mode

"POSITIVE" or "NEGATIVE", written as IONMODE=.

...

Forwarded to clean_pseudo_spectra() at "filter" and "finalize" (e.g. buffer, consensus_mz_fn, apex_source, window_mode).

Value

Invisibly tmp_dir.

Stages

prepare

Loads input, builds the feature × sample intensity matrix (featureValues(method = "medret", value = "into")), optionally subsamples with apricot, and ranks the top-top_n samples per feature (ties can add more). Writes manifest.csv, mssubset.rds, fd.rds, sample_topfeatures.rds.

sample

For one sample: extracts the MS1/MS2 scans inside each qualifying feature's chromatographic peak (± rt_buffer) and writes sample_<idx>_pool.parquet (MS2) and sample_<idx>_pointers.parquet (MS1 trace per feature).

filter

For one contiguous slice (batch_idx of n_batches) of the features: groups, scores and filters fragments with clean_pseudo_spectra() and writes features_batch_<batch_idx>.parquet.

finalize

If any features_batch_*.parquet exist in tmp_dir, binds all of them; otherwise runs the filtering for every feature in-process. Then writes the MGF with export_mgf().

all

prepare, every sample, then finalize (in-process filtering, no batches).

All stages of one run must share tmp_dir.

See also

Other api: carpediams(), process_mzml(), process_targetlist()
